behaviors.source: GH #274 "What to build"; prd.md D6; src/gate-policy.ts:1070, :1121, :154-159, :161-168, :364, :388; src/feedback-integrity-gate.ts:255, :265
behaviors.given: the new shipped file templates/quality-policy/afk.config.json, read from disk as a complete afk.config.json, and a fixture copy of it with any one member renamed to an unknown key
behaviors.when: the shipped file is passed to the production parser parseGatePolicy, and separately the renamed fixture copy is
behaviors.then: the shipped file parses without throwing and its gatePolicy carries version 1, protectedPaths with gatePolicyPaths exactly ["afk.config.json", "suite-budgets.json"] and testGlobs exactly ["**/*.test.ts"] — the shipped baselines DEFAULT_GATE_POLICY_PATHS and DEFAULT_TEST_GLOBS written out explicitly so a consuming project sees the shape it edits, gatePolicyPaths being the exact-path list the feedback-integrity gate's gate-policy risk class classifies a changed path against — riskClasses holding all four members of GATE_RISK_CLASSES, acceptance, cost and clean; and the renamed copy throws naming the offending key, because requireKnownKeys / requireExactKeys refuse an unknown member, which is why no _note-style comment member exists anywhere in the file and the tool-choice notes live in README.md instead
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts's [behavior:B-01] unit tests (no git) assert the successful parse, gatePolicyPaths and testGlobs deep-equal to those two exact arrays, the presence of all four riskClasses plus acceptance, cost and clean, and the named-key throw from the renamed fixture copy

behaviors.given: the shipped template's clean.gates list, declaring seven gates for format, lint, typecheck, changed-code coverage, complexity/CRAP, duplication and architecture rules
behaviors.when: each entry is inspected and the file is parsed
behaviors.then: there are exactly seven entries; each carries command, args, an explicit required setting and expectedCostMs; each id is namespaced (clean:format, clean:lint, clean:typecheck, clean:coverage-changed, clean:complexity, clean:duplication, clean:architecture) because RESERVED_GATE_IDS already owns the bare lint, tests and typecheck ids and parseCleanGate refuses a collision — the issue names the checks, the shipped parser names the id rule; and every entry whose named tool accepts paths carries the literal CHANGED_FILES_TOKEN {changedFiles} in args. What expectedCostMs can decide is not this behavior's claim: the non-goals hold it, guaranteed by the absence of any new reader (ADR 0063 "a wall-clock budget cannot fail a gate")
behaviors.observableResult: src/gate-policy.test.ts's [behavior:B-02] unit tests assert gates.length === 7, that every id is absent from RESERVED_GATE_IDS and collision-free, that every entry sets required, and the {changedFiles} token in args for every path-accepting entry
